cards.explanation: The answer is False. Paul, the apostle writing this letter to Timothy, says the person teaching against the sound words of our Lord Jesus Christ is "…conceited and understands nothing." He doesn't say the man has the truth and just fumbles the delivery. Teaching against those words (1 Timothy 6:3) isn't a speaking problem, friends. Paul says it's an understanding problem.

The answer is envy and strife and evil suspicions. Paul says envy, strife, abusive talk and evil suspicions come out of those controversies and disputes about words (1 Timothy 6:4). That's a whole basket of trouble, friends. Nobody walks away from a word fight with a trophy.

The answer is a means of gain. Paul says these men regard godliness as a means of gain (1 Timothy 6:5). In other words, they treat it like a way to get something. Hold onto that, friends, because Paul is about to flip it on its head in the very next verse.

The answer is nothing in and nothing out. Paul says, "For we brought nothing into the world, so we cannot carry anything out of it." (1 Timothy 6:7) Nothing in, nothing out, bakers. Not even a carry-on bag!

The answer is clothing. Paul says, "But if we have food and clothing, we will be content with these." (1 Timothy 6:8) Food and clothing, and that's the list, friends. My apron counts, and I'm very content with it.

The answer is temptation. Paul says those who want to be rich fall into temptation (1 Timothy 6:9). Notice he's talking about wanting to be rich, not the people who have a little in the cupboard. The wanting is where the falling starts, friends.

The answer is True. Paul says those foolish and harmful desires "…plunge them into ruin and destruction." (1 Timothy 6:9) Plunge is a strong word, friends, like a dive with no water at the bottom. I'm glad Paul tells us ahead of time.

The answer is love. Paul says, "For the love of money is the root of all kinds of evil." (1 Timothy 6:10) It's the love of it, not the money sitting there. A quarter in a pocket isn't the trouble, bakers. Hearts holding on too tight is what Paul has his eye on.

The answer is that they wandered away from it. Paul says that by craving money, some have wandered away from the faith (1 Timothy 6:10). It sounds quiet, like a wander and not a leap. I think that's what makes it so sneaky, friends.

The answer is that they pierced themselves. Paul says that by craving money, some have "…pierced themselves with many sorrows." (1 Timothy 6:10) Themselves! That's a hard line to read, friends. Better to catch it early.
